entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0279: Rojo development server vulnerable to DNS rebinding, allowing unauthenticated read/write access and local program execution
entry.content:
Rojo development server vulnerable to DNS rebinding, allowing unauthenticated read/write access and local program execution

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • rojo — fixed in 7.7.0

Rojo's `rojo serve` command starts an unauthenticated HTTP API on localhost (default port 34872) with no `Host` or `Origin` header validation. While direct cross-origin `fetch()` requests from a malicious website are blocked by the browser's default CORS policy, an attacker can use DNS rebinding to bypass this restriction entirely. The serve API is a two-way sync protocol. Once a DNS rebind is established, a malicious webpage visited by a developer running `rojo serve` can, without any further user interaction: - **Read the full project source:** `GET /api/rojo` returns the session ID, root instance ID, and project name. `GET /api/read/{id}` enumerates the complete instance tree including all script contents, exposing proprietary game logic, configuration, and any secrets embedde…

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/rojo
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0279.html
  • https://github.com/rojo-rbx/rojo/pull/1270
  • https://github.com/rojo-rbx/rojo/commit/ac6941f05483b0875fda52c7664cd42033db7fa2

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0281: `greentic-setup` 1.3.1-dev.34027618345 was removed from crates.io due to containing malicious code
entry.content:
`greentic-setup` 1.3.1-dev.34027618345 was removed from crates.io due to containing malicious code

Affected:

  • greentic-setup — fixed in 1.3.1-dev.34027618345.0

A new version of the `greentic-setup` crate was published with a variant of the PolinRider malware included that would fire when a project depending on `greentic-setup` was opened in Visual Studio Code. One malicious version was published on 2026-09-06, approximately 27 hours before removal. This crate is depended on by four other crates in the Greentic ecosystem, namely `greentic-start`, `greentic-start-dev`, `greentic-operator`, and `greentic-operator-dev`. We have no evidence that this crate version was downloaded by any actual users, but Greentic users should check their systems nonetheless. Thanks to the Research Team at Nextron Systems GmbH for the report.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/greentic-setup
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0281.html

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2f9f-gq7v-9h6m: Apache Thrift has a Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value Vulnerability
entry.content:
Apache Thrift has a Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value Vulnerability

Aliases: BIT-thrift-2026-43868, CVE-2026-43868

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • thrift — fixed in 0.23.0

Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value vulnerability in Apache Thrift. This issue affects Apache Thrift: before 0.23.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [0.23.0](https://github.com/apache/thrift/releases/tag/v0.23.0), which fixes the issue.
